Initial reaction rates v (uM/min) of a purified enzyme were measured at substrate concentrations S (uM) (no inhibitor, I = 0). Each condition was measured in duplicate; rates carry additive measurement noise.

The data table has 20 rows with columns: S, v. Your model will be used to predict rates at substrate levels outside the measured range.

Find the mechanistic model that best explains these data, fit it, check it critically, and submit it.

content.thinking:
Now I'm going over the rate measurements, which climb steeply at first and then level off near 10 without a clear drop at the highest values.

I'm checking Michaelis-Menten fits at a few points, but the Km values come out inconsistent, so I'm switching to a Hill model with n around 2 and K around 3. That reproduces the data reasonably well, and since the curve plateaus without declining at high substrate, I'm ruling out substrate inhibition and settling on the Hill form with Vmax near 10.2.

I'm settling on a Hill fit with the parameters around K ~3.2, n ~2, and I'm treating my confidence in it as moderate, roughly 0.6.
